title: Company AI Assistant - One place for answers
abstract: An AI assistant embedded in the company portal page that provides instant answers about policies, procedures, tools, and internal resources. It helps employees find information faster, reduces support requests, and improves productivity. E.g.:  how create expense report? where to find a technical document/download software? how change profile picture.
aiImpact: Employees spend less time searching across multiple systems or contacting support teams. The assistant provides quick, consistent answers, improves self service, accelerates onboarding, and reduces repetitive questions to HR, IT, Finance, and other support functions.
aiNovelty: Instead of searching through multiple portals, documents, and knowledge bases, employees can ask questions in natural language and receive direct answers with links to the correct systems, documents, or procedures.
aiFeasibility: The solution can be built using existing Copilot & SharePoint site technology combined with company knowledge sources. It can start with read only access to policies and documentation, then expand gradually to additional systems and capabilities.
aiFit: The solution improves employee productivity, simplifies access to company knowledge, supports digital transformation, and reduces operational overhead by making information available from a single entry point within the company portal.

title: DA Assistant: AI-Enabled Deal Analysis Automation
abstract: DA Assistant is an AI-enabled solution designed to automate and standardize Deal Analysis preparation by validating BOM data, connecting to product cost sources, applying controlled calculation logic, and creating a scalable foundation for an integrated Agent-of-Agents architecture supporting project analysis across finance, credit, RFPs, and contracts.
aiImpact: DA Assistant can reduce manual effort in Deal Analysis preparation by automating BOM validation, product cost retrieval, and direct material cost calculation. It improves reliability, traceability, and consistency by flagging missing data, abnormal cost values, and unresolved assumptions before pricing and approval discussions.
aiNovelty: The solution combines Copilot Studio, Dataverse, and Power Automate to create a finance-controlled AI assistant rather than a generic chatbot. It preserves the global costing format while applying structured logic, including Marketing Model matching and outlier-adjusted average costing across inventory organizations.
aiFeasibility: The project can start with a focused PoC using the existing Product Cost Master and standard Presales BOM format. The first MVP would validate BOM data, calculate direct material cost, and produce a finance-ready summary. External Power Platform support would accelerate setup, governance, and scalability.
aiFit: DA Assistant aligns with Ceragon’s need to improve Deal Analysis, RFP response, and project evaluation processes. It supports faster, more reliable commercial decisions and creates a scalable foundation for an Agent-of-Agents architecture integrating finance, credit, RFP, contract, and operational insights.

title: Ceragon Lightning File Manager
abstract: By treating internal desktop efficiency as a critical operational metric, we can eliminate dead time without compromising security. I have the technical capability and the security oversight required to incubate and execute this solution rapidly.
innImpact:
Business Impact & Proven ROI
 Massive Productivity Gains: This initiative scales a proven methodology. The recent file retrieval platform developed for the Sales Coordinator team successfully reduced invoice wait times from 5 minutes to 5 seconds.  
 Demonstrated Success: That single implementation eliminated approximately 492 hours of waiting time per quarter.  
 Global Scale: Expanding this efficiency from a targeted departmental solution to a global desktop utility—capitalizing on the momentum that secured the 2025 One Ceragon Award—will multiply these time savings across every department globally.
innNovelty:
Security & Technical Architecture
 Local-Only Execution: The tool will operate strictly on the local machine with no external cloud dependencies or telemetry, eliminating data exfiltration risks.
 InfoSec Governed: Architected and managed directly from an Information Security perspective to ensure the codebase and operational mechanics align with Ceragon’s highest security standards.
 Seamless Integration: Built to be lightweight, utilizing minimal system resources while outperforming native OS alternatives.
innFeasibility:
To develop and deploy a blazing-fast, custom file manager that operates completely locally on all corporate devices.
When paired with the recently implemented high-speed file searching tool, this will create a comprehensive, zero-latency file ecosystem. This combination will radically improve the daily user experience and instantly resolve existing complaints regarding system sluggishness.
innFit:
Problem Statement
Employees across Ceragon rely heavily on continuous file exploration, organization, and retrieval. Currently, the default Windows file manager suffers from sluggish performance and significant latency. These micro-delays compound throughout the day, creating chronic inefficiencies and generating frequent user experience complaints.

title: Stirling AI PDF as a Secure, Local Self-Hosted PDF Processing Platform for Ceragon
abstract: A Ceragon-controlled document intelligence and processing platform that reduces third-party exposure while improving employee productivity.oductivity.
aiImpact:
Ceragon employees routinely require PDF editing, merging, splitting, compression, conversion, OCR, redaction, document comparison and signing. Today, these requirements are fulfilled through a fragmented combination of desktop applications, external signing platforms and public PDF-processing websites.

Internal Defender telemetry demonstrates active use of at least 15 external PDF web applications. The observed activity includes 277 Smallpdf transactions across 49 users and 93 MB uploaded to Pdf2go. This creates a measurable risk that confidential documents may leave Ceragon’s controlled environment during routine business operations.

The proposed Ceragon Local AI Document Manager would provide one internally hosted and governed platform for PDF processing, private AI document assistance and signing workflows. Confidential files would remain within Ceragon-controlled infrastructure, significantly reducing third-party exposure and shadow-IT usage.

Expected outcomes include:

Reduction of confidential-document uploads to public PDF websites
Faster access to common PDF tools
Consolidation of fragmented PDF utilities
Private AI summarization, extraction, classification and comparison
Secure internal signing and approval workflows
Reduced dependency on external SaaS platforms
Centralized access control, auditing, retention and monitoring
Improved employee experience and document-processing efficiency

Success would be measured through external upload reduction, platform adoption, task completion time, signing cycle time, user satisfaction and security-policy compliance.
aiNovelty:
The proposed solution is not simply another PDF editor. It combines three capabilities into a unified, internally governed document platform:

A self-hosted PDF-processing foundation
A private AI document-intelligence layer
Identity-backed signing and approval workflows

Traditional PDF tools address individual operations, while public services require users to upload documents to third-party infrastructure. The Ceragon Local AI Document Manager would keep document processing and AI inference within Ceragon’s controlled environment.

The private AI layer would support authorized use cases such as:

Document summarization
Key-information extraction
Contract and policy comparison
Document classification
OCR-assisted analysis
Metadata extraction
Sensitive-information identification
Redaction recommendations
Natural-language document search
Signing-field recommendations

The platform’s main differentiator is the combination of broad PDF functionality, private AI, enterprise identity, auditability and internal data sovereignty through one Ceragon-managed user experience.
aiFeasibility:
The scope is realistic because the proposal builds on an actively maintained, open-source PDF-processing foundation rather than developing every PDF capability from scratch.

Stirling PDF already supports more than 60 PDF tools, locally hosted processing, automatic file deletion, Docker and Kubernetes deployment, SSO, user management, permission controls, API integration and batch processing.

A controlled 12-week proof of concept is proposed:

Phase 1: Security and Architecture Design, Weeks 1–2
Define approved use cases
Complete threat modeling
Establish data-classification restrictions
Review application dependencies and licenses
Design network segmentation
Define document retention and deletion requirements
Establish signing and audit requirements
Phase 2: Secure Deployment, Weeks 3–5
Deploy the platform in a segregated internal environment
Integrate Entra ID or corporate SSO
Implement role-based access
Configure TLS and certificate management
Restrict internet egress
Enable centralized security logging
Configure malware scanning and secure file deletion
Phase 3: AI and Workflow Extension, Weeks 6–8
Integrate an approved private language model
Implement document summarization and extraction
Introduce document comparison
Add policy-controlled AI prompts
Develop signing and approval workflows
Test API-based automation
Phase 4: Controlled Pilot, Weeks 9–12
Select pilot users from Legal, Finance, Sales Operations and IT
Measure user adoption and task-completion time
Perform vulnerability and penetration testing
Validate document deletion and access controls
Measure reduction in external PDF-service usage
Produce a production-readiness recommendation
Proposed Success Criteria
No unauthorized internet egress
No supported documents uploaded to external services
SSO and role-based access enforced
Document deletion technically verified
AI responses traceable to source documents
At least 70% pilot adoption
Positive user satisfaction
Measurable reduction in processing time
aiFit:
The proposal directly supports Ceragon’s security, operational-efficiency and employee-experience priorities.

Ceragon processes sensitive commercial, financial, customer, legal, technical and operational documents. Moving routine document operations into a Ceragon-controlled platform reduces the risk of confidential information being uploaded to public websites or processed by unmanaged third parties.

The solution supports Ceragon by:

Protecting intellectual property and confidential information
Reducing shadow IT and uncontrolled SaaS usage
Providing employees with a fast and trusted alternative
Standardizing document-processing workflows
Supporting data sovereignty and internal governance
Reducing fragmented software deployment and maintenance
Enabling secure automation through APIs
Establishing a reusable private-AI document capability
Improving signing and approval turnaround time

The solution would primarily improve internal employee operations, but the resulting protection of customer information, contracts and technical records would also strengthen Ceragon’s customer trust and security posture.

title: Intelligent Traffic-Aware Carrier reduction for Energy-Efficient Backhaul Links
abstract: Implement dynamic carrier on/off switching to consolidate traffic onto the minimum number of carriers during low-utilization periods and restore capacity as demand increases, reducing energy consumption and operational costs. The solution leverages an FPGA-based edge AI engine located near the traffic source for fast, real-time decision making.
innImpact:
Reduce power consumption by disabling unused radio carriers during low utilization.

Lab PoC indicates approximately 10.5 Watt saving per node (~21 W per link) for an IP-50CX 2+0 configuration. 
Expected around 25 Watt power saving when using Microwave RFU-D-HP node (50Watts for link).

Contributing to:
Lower operational expenses (OPEX).

Reduced thermal stress and potentially longer equipment lifespan.
Improved sustainability and energy efficiency for operators.
innNovelty:
Current microwave links typically operate at full carrier configuration regardless of actual traffic demand.

This solution introduces:
Automatic carrier-level energy optimization.
Traffic-aware on/off switching between single and dual/multiple carrier operation.
Future predictive AI capability that can proactively prepare the network for expected traffic changes.
Using a dedicated efficient Adge AI computing, implemented in HW FPGA device near the traffic.
The combination of power saving and service-aware operation creates a practical Green Mode capability for backhaul. networks.
innFeasibility:
Validation Approach:
Implement Scheduled Carrier Switching as an initial PoC.

Define safe switching procedures and recovery mechanisms.

Verify seamless carrier restoration during traffic spikes.

Measure actual power savings in lab and field deployments.

Resources & Timeline:
Software development in network management, EMS and radio control components.
Lab validation work and might followed by limited customer / Beta sites trials.
Phased implementation from scheduled mode to dynamic traffic-aware mode.
innFit:
The solution aligns with Ceragon's goals of improving network efficiency and delivering innovative backhaul capabilities.
Benefits include:
Added value for mobile network operators.
Reduced customer operating costs
Support for sustainability and energy-saving initiatives.
Can be integrated into existing Ceragon management and radio platforms.
This feature strengthens Ceragon's competitive position by offering a practical energy-efficiency capability without requiring new hardware.

title: Supplier Payment Process Improvement
abstract:
To implement a centralized vendor portal that enables suppliers to upload shipment information and invoices through an Advance Shipment Notice (ASN) process while automating notifications and document flow across Warehouse, SCM, and Finance teams.
The solution will provide real-time shipment visibility, automate document sharing, and streamline the vendor payment process.
innImpact:
Project Background-: Currently, there is no centralized platform to track inbound vendor shipments. Shipment notifications, invoice submissions, and document sharing are managed through manual email communication between suppliers and internal stakeholders. Once materials are received at the warehouse, the Warehouse team manually shares Goods Receipt Note (GRN) details and supporting documents with the Finance team to initiate vendor payments.
This process results in:
•	Limited visibility of inbound shipments.
•	Dependency on manual communication and follow-ups.
•	Delayed document sharing and payment processing.
•	Increased risk of missing documentation.
•	Lack of real-time collaboration among Suppliers, Warehouse, SCM, and Finance teams.

Proposed Solution:- Develop a web-based Vendor Portal with the following capabilities:
Supplier Activities
•	Upload Advance Shipment Notice (ASN).
•	Upload Invoice and supporting shipment documents.
•	Track shipment and document submission status.
Automated Workflow
1.	Supplier submits ASN, invoice, and supporting documents through the portal.
2.	Automated notifications are sent to: 
o	Warehouse Team
o	Supply Chain Management Team
o	Finance Team
3.	Warehouse team gains advance visibility of incoming shipments and can plan resources accordingly.
4.	Upon material receipt, Warehouse team performs Goods Receipt (GRN) and updates status in the portal.
5.	Finance team receives automated notification along with GRN confirmation and supporting documents.
6.	Payment processing is initiated without manual intervention from the Warehouse team.
innNovelty:
To implement a centralized vendor portal that enables suppliers to upload shipment information and invoices through an Advance Shipment Notice (ASN) process while automating notifications and document flow across Warehouse, SCM, and Finance teams.
The solution will provide real-time shipment visibility, automate document sharing, and streamline the vendor payment process
innFeasibility: We are not planning to change any financial process, just try to reduce the manual work to automated.
innFit: The proposed Vendor Shipment Visibility Portal will establish a digital, transparent, and automated process from shipment dispatch through payment initiation. The solution will improve operational efficiency, enhance warehouse planning, accelerate finance processing, reduce manual effort, and create a seamless collaboration platform for suppliers and internal stakeholders.

title: NetMaster Lifecycle Intelligence & Upgrade Recommendation
abstract: Enhance NetMaster with continuous lifecycle intelligence to identify Out of Support and End of Life equipment, notify customers of lifecycle risks, and recommend suitable replacement solutions. This will enable proactive network modernization, improve customer visibility, reduce operational risks, and create new opportunities for upgrades, upselling, and network transformation.
innImpact:
Significance of the Problem

Customers often lack clear and continuous visibility into the lifecycle status of equipment deployed in their networks. Out of Support or End of Life equipment may remain in operation without the customer being fully aware of the associated support, availability, and operational risks. Today, identifying such equipment and planning replacements can require manual analysis and coordination, making the process reactive rather than proactive.

Expected Outcomes

The proposed NetMaster capability would provide continuous lifecycle visibility and proactively identify equipment approaching or already in OoS/EoL status. It would:

Reduce the risk associated with unsupported or obsolete equipment.
Help customers proactively plan network upgrades and modernization.
Provide recommended replacement solutions, reducing the effort required to identify upgrade paths.
Improve customer awareness and engagement around network lifecycle management.
Create new opportunities for equipment upgrades, upselling, and network modernization.
Position NetMaster as a more proactive network lifecycle management and business-enablement platform, rather than only a network monitoring and inventory tool.
innNovelty:
The novelty is in integrating equipment lifecycle intelligence directly into NetMaster, rather than relying on separate lifecycle databases, manual checks, or commercial assessments.

NetMaster would proactively identify OoS/EoL equipment within the live managed network and link each affected element to a recommended replacement or upgrade path. This combines network management, lifecycle visibility, and modernization recommendations in a single platform.

The approach would shift lifecycle management from a reactive, manual process to a proactive and automated capability, creating value for both customers and the business.
innFeasibility:
es. The proposed functionality is realistic and achievable using existing NetMaster capabilities and available data sources.

The solution can leverage existing inventory, device identification, and database mechanisms to identify OoS/EoL equipment, display lifecycle status, provide notifications, and recommend replacement products where applicable.

The main dependency is having an accurate and regularly maintained database of product lifecycle information and recommended replacements.

Overall, the project is technically feasible and can be implemented incrementally, with the potential to evolve into a broader NetMaster lifecycle management capability.
innFit:
The project supports the company’s focus on customer value, network modernization, digitalization, and revenue growth.

It strengthens NetMaster as a strategic network management platform by providing customers with proactive lifecycle visibility and actionable upgrade recommendations. At the same time, it supports tactical priorities by helping identify upgrade, upsell, and modernization opportunities based on the actual equipment deployed in customer networks.

The solution also promotes proactive customer engagement, reduces the risks associated with obsolete equipment, and encourages migration toward newer, supported technologies.

title: AI-Powered Telecom Network Monitoring, RCA & Voice Assistant
abstract: An AI-enabled telecom network monitoring platform that provides real-time visibility of network links, intelligent alarm analysis, root cause identification, and voice-based interaction. The solution consolidates NMS data, identifies issues such as link failures, node disconnections, RSL and XPI conditions, and enables faster operational decision-making.
aiImpact: The solution reduces manual monitoring effort by providing centralized network visibility, faster issue identification and intelligent RCA support. It can improve response time, reduce operational dependency on manual analysis, and help network teams make faster, data-driven decisions.
aiNovelty: The solution combines real-time NMS monitoring, network alarm interpretation, RCA and voice-based AI interaction in a single operational interface. Instead of requiring engineers to manually correlate multiple network conditions, the assistant converts network data into actionable insights through natural-language interaction.
aiFeasibility: The solution is built around existing NMS data and operational workflows, making it practical to integrate with the current network monitoring environment. The modular architecture allows AI capabilities, dashboards and automation features to be introduced incrementally without requiring major changes to the underlying network infrastructure.
aiFit: The solution aligns with Ceragon’s focus on intelligent network operations, automation and improved customer experience. By enhancing network visibility, accelerating fault analysis and enabling AI-assisted operations, it can support efficient NMS operations and scalable service assurance for telecom networks.

title: MindLog AI: Intelligent Log Analysis for Faster Troubleshooting
abstract: MindLog AI uses natural language processing and automated pattern detection to analyze technical logs, identify significant events, and generate structured troubleshooting reports. It reduces manual investigation effort, improves consistency, and helps support engineers reach evidence-based conclusions faster while retaining human validation of the final findings.
aiImpact: Technical log analysis is often time-consuming and dependent on individual expertise. MindLog AI reduces the effort required to review large log files by highlighting significant events, patterns, anomalies, and relevant time correlations. Expected outcomes include faster troubleshooting, more consistent investigations, improved knowledge sharing, and reduced risk of overlooking important evidence.
aiNovelty: MindLog AI combines log parsing, configurable keyword intelligence, pattern detection, PM analysis, AI-generated explanations, and structured reporting in a workflow designed specifically for technical support investigations. Unlike generic log-search tools, it converts raw evidence into prioritized and readable findings while preserving the original log context for engineering validation.
aiFeasibility: A working solution has already been developed and can be demonstrated using anonymized technical logs. The project can be expanded incrementally by adding supported log formats, improving event correlation, validating results against engineer-led investigations, and incorporating feedback from support and R&D teams.
aiFit: MindLog AI supports Ceragon’s operational and customer-support priorities by accelerating technical investigations, improving analysis consistency, and helping engineers reuse troubleshooting knowledge. The solution can support Customer Support, R&D, QA, integration, and field teams while improving case-handling efficiency and the quality of technical reports. It also can be use as a tool for network audit.

title: Quote-to-Order Automation: Connecting Salesforce, Partner Portal & Oracle
abstract: Today, a signed contract takes six manual handoffs: email, Excel, re-entry — before reaching Oracle. This project connects Salesforce, the Partner Portal, and Oracle so clients submit their BOM/PO directly, pre-filled with account data. The PO auto-pushes to Oracle, and Salesforce status updates itself — no manual entry, no delay
innImpact: Every PO currently passes through six manual handoffs, adding days of delay, error risk, and no real-time Salesforce visibility — while a full Orders team is dedicated to re-entry work a system could do instantly. Automating this cuts time-to-revenue, removes duplicate data entry, and frees the Orders team to focus on true exceptions instead of routine processing.
innNovelty: Rather than adding another manual checkpoint or a generic ERP integration, this approach uses data Salesforce already holds (VAT, tax, currency) to eliminate re-entry entirely, and ties Salesforce's opportunity status directly to a real business event (PO receipt) instead of a manual update. The BOM Validation and Orders teams' manual steps are removed, not just streamlined.
innFeasibility: The integration relies on standard, well-understood tools already used at enterprise scale — either a native Oracle-Salesforce adapter, MuleSoft (Salesforce's own iPaaS), or a custom API integration against both systems' REST APIs. No new platform purchase is required. A phased pilot (2–3 accounts) lets IT validate data mapping and business rules before full rollout.
innFit: This directly supports the quote-to-cash motion — a core, cross-functional sales operations priority — by removing friction between Sales, CSM, and Orders. It reduces operational cost through better resource allocation, improves partner/customer experience with faster order confirmation, and strengthens Salesforce as the single source of truth for pipeline status.

title: Intelligent Traffic-Aware Carrier reduction for Energy-Efficient Backhaul Links
abstract: Implement dynamic carrier on/off switching to consolidate traffic onto theminimum number of carriers during low-utilization periods and restore capacityas demand increases, reducing energy consumption and operational costs. Thesolution leverages an FPGA-based edge AI engine located near the traffic sourcefor fast, real-time decision making.
innImpact:
Customer Benefits:
Reduced power consumption across microwave deployments,
Lower network operating costs (OPEX),
Improved sustainability and ESG metrics
Extended equipment lifespan through lower thermal stress.
Ceragon Benefits:
Differentiating Green Networking capability,
Strong value proposition for operators seeking energy-efficient infrastructure,
Increased competitiveness in new opportunities and tenders.
Measured Lab Results:
Initial PoC showed approximately 10.5W power reduction per node for IP-50CX,
Approximately 21W power reduction per link in a 2+0 configuration,

The feature is customer-facing, applicable across multiple product families, and aligns with both near-term product enhancement goals and long-term intelligent networking vision.

title: Lead & Partner Workflow Automation: AI-Assisted Follow-Up Across HubSpot, Salesforce & Outlook
abstract: EMEA/LATAM Inside Sales handles too many leads across Salesforce, events, and outbound to track manually. This project uses AI to draft follow-up emails on unanswered leads, on a cadence I set, approved before sending — plus routes existing-client requests to account owners and gates new leads to company emails only.
aiImpact: Untracked leads across Salesforce, events, and outbound mean missed follow-ups and lost pipeline — with no system flagging who needs contact, or when. Automating follow-up ensures zero leads go cold, cuts existing-client routing from days to minutes, and gives Inside Sales a consistent, scalable process across EMEA and LATAM.
aiNovelty: Unlike generic sales-cadence tools that auto-send on a fixed schedule, this approach keeps a human in the loop: AI drafts each follow-up using the lead's actual history and source context, but nothing sends without my review and approval. It also solves a root-cause gap most tools miss — the BCC email-to-Salesforce workaround that hides client replies — by replacing it with a clean CC alias, so the AI's "no reply" signal is actually accurate instead of guessed.
aiFeasibility: Yes — this relies on capabilities Claude already supports natively: a Salesforce connector, a recurring task to check for unanswered leads, and human approval before sending, with no new platform purchase required. The scope is phased: Phase 1 connects Salesforce and defines cadence/approval rules, Phase 2 pilots on a subset of leads for 2–4 weeks, and only after that does IT add the configuration-only workflows (routing, email-domain gate, partner vetting).
aiFit: This directly supports revenue growth in EMEA and LATAM by ensuring no lead goes untracked, while giving Inside Sales a repeatable, scalable process instead of manual tracking that doesn't grow with volume. It strengthens Salesforce as the single source of pipeline truth, reduces friction for existing clients reaching their account owner, and sets a consistent, auditable bar for who becomes a partner — all while keeping a human approving every customer-facing message.

title: Site Vision AI by IA.
abstract:
AI trains on Ceragon's millions of installation photos to automatic QA every deployment in real time, inside, whilethe crew is still onsite eliminating revisits, enabling 100% QA coverage, and auto-approving siteentry.
Ceragon reviews only a smallsample of installations, and always after the crew has left, so defects become costly siterevisits
innImpact:
Why the problem matters
•	Site revisits are pure waste. Every avoidable revisit costs roughly [$Z] in crew time, travel, permits and site access — and consumes capacity we could be using on new sites. Across [N] sites per year with a [R]% defect-driven revisit rate, that is a material annual cost, borne by Ceragon or by our subcontractors (and priced back into their rates either way).
•	Hidden defects are worse than known ones. With only [X]% coverage we are quality-assuring a sample and hoping it represents the rest. Undetected grounding and sealing defects are the classic root cause of lightning damage, water ingress and intermittent link degradation — failures that surface as customer escalations, warranty work and truck rolls long after project close.
•	Delayed acceptance delays revenue. Every QA finding and revisit pushes out customer site acceptance, which pushes out milestone billing and cash collection.
•	Crews idle at the gate. Site-entry approval waits are unbillable, unproductive time for every crew in every country where the process applies, and a scheduling risk when approvals arrive late in the day.


Beyond the direct savings
•	First-time-right delivery becomes a measurable, provable claim in customer reviews and in bids — a differentiator, not a promise.
•	Genuinely better networks. 100% inspection lifts the quality floor of every site we hand over, reducing post-deployment failures and improving link availability for the customer.
•	Faster site acceptance improves services margin and cash conversion on turnkey programmes.
•	Subcontractor performance becomes visible and objective. Per-crew, per-partner and per-region quality scorecards based on evidence rather than sampling, usable in vendor management and rate negotiation.
•	Scalable capacity. We can grow deployment volume without growing QA headcount linearly.
•	Safety and compliance. Consistent, documented, auditable verification of PPE and entry procedures on every single site visit instead of a variable human check.
•	Institutional knowledge captured. Our senior deployment engineers' judgement is encoded into a system that every crew, including new subcontractors in new markets, benefits from on day one.
innNovelty:
What makes SiteVision AI novel
•	QA moves from audit to prevention. The novelty is not "AI looks at photos" — it is when it looks. Inspection happens at the moment of capture, while the crew, the ladder or on the tower during the installation and the tools are still on site. That single shift converts a detection process into a prevention process and structurally removes the revisit.
•	Domain-specific, checkpoint-aware intelligence. The model does not classify "good site / bad site". It evaluates a specific checkpoint against Ceragon's deployment guides: grounding bonding method and conductor path, connector weatherproofing, cable bend radius and tie-down spacing, ODU/antenna mounting and alignment, waveguide dressing, labelling. This encodes Ceragon engineering standards, not generic computer vision.
•	A proprietary data asset no vendor can replicate. Millions of microwave and mmWave installation images, already tagged by checkpoint through the InSite form structure and partially adjudicated by our own QA engineers. This is a genuine competitive moat, and it already exists, so we are not starting from zero.
•	A self-improving closed loop. Our existing human QA process becomes the labelling engine. Every escalated case makes the model better; coverage and accuracy compound over time instead of plateauing.
•	Zero new tools for the field. It runs inside the InSite mobile app that installers and subcontractors already use. No adoption programmed, no new login, no change to how a crew works.
the highest-risk failure mode of most field-AI projects is designed out.
•	One engine, two processes. The same platform governs both entry to the site (safety and compliance pre-check) and exit from the site (installation quality).
the two human review bottlenecks that bracket every deployment.
innFeasibility:
Yes — because the three things that usually kill this kind of project are already solved at Ceragon.

•	The data exists. Millions of historical images, structured by checkpoint, with existing QA verdicts on the sampled portion. No data-collection programme, no waiting.
•	The delivery channel exists. InSite already captures the photos with their form context and already uploads them. We are adding a scoring service and a result indicator, not building an application.
•	The expertise exists. Our deployment QA engineers and regional installation leads are the subject-matter experts who define what "good" looks like and adjudicate edge cases.
innFit:
Alignment with Ceragon's strategic and tactical priorities.
Strategic alignment
•	Profitable growth in services. Deployment and turnkey services carry the thinnest margins and the highest execution risk in our portfolio. Revisits, rework and delayed acceptance hit that margin directly. SiteVision AI attacks the largest controllable cost in the services P&L.
•	Scaling delivery without scaling headcount. As we take on larger multi-site programmes and new geographies, QA capacity is a hard constraint. Automating inspection lets deployment volume grow faster than the organisation.
•	Quality as a competitive differentiator. "100% of sites inspected, AI-verified, first-time-right" is a concrete, auditable claim in RFP responses and QBRs — particularly with tier-1 operators and in markets where installation quality determines vendor selection.
•	Company-wide AI adoption, done properly. This is exactly the kind of AI use case INNO.LAB is asking for: a real bottleneck, a proprietary data asset, a measurable business outcome, and a repeatable pattern. The same shape — documented process, photo evidence, human reviewer — appears in maintenance, upgrades, spares inspection and network audits. Phase 1 builds the platform for all of them.
•	Turning execution culture into a technology asset. Ceragon's strength is execution. This encodes that execution standard into software so it applies uniformly across every crew, every subcontractor and every market, and improves over time.
Tactical alignment
•	Direct, near-term cost reduction: fewer revisits, less QA labour per site, less unproductive crew waiting time at site gates.
•	Faster cash conversion: faster QA verdicts, faster customer acceptance, faster milestone billing.
•	Customer satisfaction and trust: fewer defects handed over, fewer escalations, a better first-time-right record.
•	Safety and regulatory compliance: consistent, documented verification of entry procedures and protective equipment on every visit.
•	Better partner management: objective, evidence-based quality scorecards per subcontractor and region.
•	Leverages existing investment: builds on InSite, our existing QA organisation and our existing image archive, rather than buying a new platform.

title: From Manual Handoffs to Real-Time Order Flow
abstract: Today, a signed contract takes six manual handoffs: email, Excel, re-entry — before reaching Oracle. This project connects Salesforce, the Partner Portal, and Oracle so clients submit their BOM/PO directly, pre-filled with account data. The PO auto-pushes to Oracle, and Salesforce status updates itself — no manual entry, no delay.
innImpact: Every PO currently passes through six manual handoffs, adding days of delay, error risk, and no real-time Salesforce visibility — while a full Orders team is dedicated to re-entry work a system could do instantly. Automating this cuts time-to-revenue, removes duplicate data entry, and frees the Orders team to focus on true exceptions instead of routine processing.
innNovelty: Rather than adding another manual checkpoint or a generic ERP integration, this approach uses data Salesforce already holds (VAT, tax, currency) to eliminate re-entry entirely, and ties Salesforce's opportunity status directly to a real business event (PO receipt) instead of a manual update. The BOM Validation and Orders teams' manual steps are removed, not just streamlined.
innFeasibility: The integration relies on standard, well-understood tools already used at enterprise scale — either a native Oracle-Salesforce adapter, MuleSoft (Salesforce's own iPaaS), or a custom API integration against both systems' REST APIs. No new platform purchase is required. A phased pilot (2–3 accounts) lets IT validate data mapping and business rules before full rollout.
innFit: This directly supports the quote-to-cash motion — a core, cross-functional sales operations priority — by removing friction between Sales, CSM, and Orders. It reduces operational cost through better resource allocation, improves partner/customer experience with faster order confirmation, and strengthens Salesforce as the single source of truth for pipeline status.

title: High-capacity transport aggregation node
abstract: High-capacity transport aggregation node: modification of products like IP-50GP, IP-50GPX and similar future products (with higher-speed interfaces). Potential customers: CSPs and WISPs or  vendors that do not directly compete with us WITH similar needs: FSO providers, FWA vendors (like RADWIN, Mimosa, Ubiquity) and Private Networks using FSO, fiber, private 5G.
innImpact: We can aggregate traffic from multiple links, FWA solutions etc, and provide to them high-speed interface towards the network such as 25 GbE interfaces (50 GbE, 100 GbE in the future). We can split the traffic in a sophisticated way, provide redundancy etc.
innNovelty: Generic Ethernet switch is probably not attractive, but a wireless-aware aggregation platform derived from IP-50GP/IP-50GPX could be a credible adjacent market for Ceragon, particularly targeting FSO and private network operators. Our radio-aware capabilities such as L1 aggregation or support in sync protocols may create a benefit here. Unlike the big generic switch vendors, we have the know-how and we may also "tailor" specific solutions to customers.
innFeasibility: IP-50GP/IP-50GPX, our L1 aggregation (proved to work with third parties) and sync protocol support should be a great base.
innFit: Additional revenues, low-hanging fruits, extremely relevant for CSPs/ISPs but also matches the end-to-end solutions that PN are looking for - also providing something integrators cannot do.
